name: Lazy loading
explanation: Loading images, components or data only when they are needed, for example when they scroll into view.
triggers: load later;only when needed;faster page load;load on scroll;page loads slowly;big images;scroll into view;visible on screen;load images;takes forever;slow to load
requirements: Add loading=lazy to images and iframes further down the page, not to the main top image;Reserve space with width and height so content does not jump when it loads;Load heavy components and routes on demand with dynamic import;Show a placeholder or skeleton while lazy content loads;Start loading a little before content scrolls into view
done_when: The first screen loads quickly and its main image is not delayed;Scrolling never shows layout jumps or long-empty gaps

name: Debouncing and throttling
explanation: Limiting how often a function runs, for example waiting until the user stops typing before sending a search request.
triggers: stop typing;every keystroke;while typing;search as you type;too many calls
requirements: Debounce search as you type, sending a request after a pause of about 200 to 300 ms;Throttle scroll and resize handlers, or use requestAnimationFrame;Ignore or cancel responses to outdated requests so old results never replace new ones;Run the action immediately on Enter or submit, without waiting for the delay
done_when: Typing quickly sends one request, not one per keystroke;Results always match the latest text typed

name: Browser storage
explanation: Saving small amounts of data in the browser with localStorage, sessionStorage, IndexedDB or cookies so it survives a page reload.
triggers: remember;after refresh;save in the browser;keep after reload;remember my settings;still there after reload
requirements: Never keep passwords, tokens or personal data in localStorage, which any script can read;Wrap reads and writes in try and catch, because storage can be full or blocked;Store only small values there, and use IndexedDB for larger data;Version stored data so older formats can be migrated or cleared;Keep the server as the source of truth for anything important
done_when: The app still works when storage is disabled or cleared;No secrets are visible in the browser's storage panel

name: Event handling
explanation: Running code in response to user actions such as clicks, typing or form submission, by attaching event listeners to elements.
triggers: button does nothing;nothing happens when;does nothing;click doesn't work;not responding to clicks;when i click the button
requirements: Use real buttons and links for actions, so keyboard and screen readers work;Remove listeners when their element or component is removed;Use event delegation for long or changing lists;Prevent double submission by disabling the button while an action runs;Prevent the browser's default behaviour only when you replace it
done_when: Every action works with mouse, keyboard and touch;Clicking twice quickly never sends two requests

name: Internationalization (i18n)
explanation: Preparing an app for several languages and regions, with translated text, local date and number formats, and right-to-left layouts.
triggers: other languages;multiple languages;translate the app;in spanish;in french;another language;different languages
requirements: Keep all user-facing text in translation files, never hard-coded;Use placeholders with plural rules instead of joining strings together;Format dates, numbers and currencies for the user's locale with the Intl API;Set the lang attribute, and support right-to-left layouts where needed;Leave room in the layout for longer translations
done_when: Switching language changes every visible text;Dates, numbers and plurals look right in each language

name: Dates and time zones
explanation: Storing times in UTC and showing them in each user's local time zone and format, using tools such as the Intl API or date-fns.
triggers: local time;convert the date;date format;wrong time;time difference;format the date
requirements: Store times in UTC, or with an explicit offset;Convert to the user's time zone only when displaying;Store future events with their time zone name, so daylight saving changes work;Use a date library or the Intl API instead of calculating by hand;Treat date-only values such as birthdays as dates, not timestamps
done_when: Users in different time zones see the same event at their correct local time;Daylight saving changes never shift saved times

name: Search engine optimization (SEO)
explanation: Helping search engines find and show your pages, with good titles, meta descriptions, a sitemap, fast loading and server-side rendering.
triggers: show up on google;rank on google;found on google;google search;link preview;share preview
requirements: Give every page a unique title and meta description;Use one h1 and a logical heading structure;Put content in the HTML, with server-side rendering or pre-rendering for key pages;Add a sitemap.xml and a robots.txt, and set canonical URLs;Add Open Graph tags for link previews
done_when: Search engines can read the page content without running JavaScript;Sharing a link shows the right title, description and image

name: Image optimization
explanation: Making images load faster by resizing and compressing them, using modern formats like WebP or AVIF, and serving the right size for each screen.
triggers: images make the page slow;images are slow;images are too big;compress images;image size;heavy images;images load slowly
requirements: Serve modern formats such as WebP or AVIF, with a fallback;Resize images, and use srcset and sizes to serve the right size for each screen;Set width and height to prevent layout shift;Lazy-load images further down the page, but not the main image at the top;Give meaningful images alt text, and decorative ones an empty alt
done_when: No image is much larger than its displayed size;Screen readers describe meaningful images and skip decorative ones

name: Offline support
explanation: Keeping an app usable without an internet connection by storing files and data on the device, usually with a service worker, and syncing changes later.
triggers: without internet;no internet;no connection;work offline;bad connection;lost connection;sync later;install the app
requirements: Cache the app shell and key files with a service worker;Show clearly when the user is offline;Queue changes made offline and sync them when back online;Resolve conflicts when the same data changed elsewhere meanwhile;Version the cache so updates replace old files
done_when: The app opens and shows saved data without a connection;Changes made offline are saved once the connection returns

name: Web performance (Core Web Vitals)
explanation: Making pages load fast, respond quickly and stay visually stable, as measured by Google's Core Web Vitals.
triggers: page is slow;site is slow;speed score;slow website;improve performance;make the page faster;load faster;janky;lighthouse score;feels slow
requirements: Aim for Largest Contentful Paint at most 2.5 s, Interaction to Next Paint at most 200 ms, layout shift at most 0.1;Measure at the 75th percentile of real visits, on mobile and desktop separately;Collect real user data, such as with the web-vitals library or CrUX, not only lab tests;Make the main image load early with fetchpriority=high, and never lazy-load it;Break up long JavaScript tasks and ship less JavaScript, so the page responds quickly;Reserve space for images, ads and embeds to stop layout shift;Keep Time to First Byte low with caching and a CDN;Inline critical CSS, load other CSS without blocking, and load scripts with defer or async
done_when: All three Core Web Vitals are in the good range at the 75th percentile;Real user data, not just Lighthouse, confirms the result

name: Language selector
explanation: A control that lets users switch the website or app to another language.
triggers: change language;change the language;switch language;switch the language;choose language;select language;language menu;view in spanish
requirements: Show each language name in that language, such as Deutsch rather than German;Do not use flags to represent languages;Set the lang attribute on each option;Remember the choice and keep the user on the same page after switching;Put the language in the URL, such as /fr/, so each version can be indexed;Link language versions with hreflang;Place it where people expect, usually in the header or footer
done_when: Switching language keeps the user on the equivalent page;Users who cannot read the current language can still find their own;Search engines find every language version
